gestures.body: Just two gestures: tap and long-press.
gestures.callout:
Tap handles most meals.
Long-press only when you had something different or want more detail.

ingredients.body: Each button groups foods commonly eaten in Japan. The calorie value logged on tap stays close to a typical portion.
ingredients.footnote1: Top foods are selected based on consumption share within each category in Japan's National Health and Nutrition Survey (NHNS).
ingredients.footnote2: Buttons labelled "long-press" require a selection each time because the calorie range varies significantly by type.

dishes.body: Dish buttons log a representative value for a complete meal. Pick the dish closest to what you ate.
dishes.footnote1: Many dish buttons (set meals, sushi, pizza, ramen, etc.) have a wide calorie range, so long-press is the default for those.
dishes.footnote2: Soups such as miso soup and tonjiru are under "Set meal / Single dish / Soup".

future.body: The more you log, the easier it becomes to find your go-to foods and dishes.
future.starBody: Switch to the ⭐️ tab to see your most-used items at the top. Tap straight through your usual combination without searching.
future.defaultBody: The tab shown when you open the app automatically shifts to whichever tab you use most.

faq.q1: What if the portion isn't exactly right?
faq.a1: Logging at a standard serving is fine. You can adjust to large or small after tapping. The design prioritizes "easy to keep up" over precision.
faq.q2: Isn't one button too rough with multiple foods inside?
faq.a2: Foods within each button are chosen so that typical portions land in roughly the same calorie range as the tap value. You can check the range in the "Ingredient button contents" and "Dish button contents" steps.
faq.q3: Can't I log with a photo?
faq.a3: Photo → recognition → confirmation adds friction that makes it hard to sustain. A few taps is all it takes, so you can log every day without effort.
faq.q4: What if I want more precise tracking?
faq.a4: This app is designed around "roughly, consistently". For gram-level precision, pairing with a food-composition app (e.g. Asken) works well.

data.title: Data
data.body1: Hachibu works without an account — your data is stored only on this device. Deleting the app or switching phones will erase your meal logs, weight, and body fat records.
data.body2: Subscriptions are tied to your Apple ID / Google Account. You can restore a previous purchase from the Subscription screen after reinstalling.
